memory_candidates.content: A coarse `grep -rlE '\\b'` sweep for word-boundary construct sites produces false positives that must be filtered by inspection, not assumed real: LaTeX/Typst macros (`\begin`, `\bf`, `\bigl`, `\bullet`, `\binom`, `\bot`, `\boldsymbol`, `\bibliography`, `\bottomrule`) match the substring `\`+`b`; literal escaped strings in test fixtures (e.g. a jq string containing `\\backslash`) match the same way; and `sed`/Python `re` calls use `\b` under a completely different, non-ugrep-affected engine. Before counting a hit as a genuine at-risk grep site, confirm it is (a) a live `grep`/`egrep` invocation, not dead code or a doc-example echo, and (b) actually the construct in question, not a substring coincidence.

When landing a new agent-system/extensions/core/context/standards/*.md file and indexing it in index-entries.json, the source-store copies of check-extension-docs.sh and generate-context-line-counts.sh both self-refuse when run directly from agent-system/extensions/core/scripts (they detect the source-store tree and require the deployed .claude/scripts/ copy, or a REPO_ROOT override). The reliable sequence is: add the index entry, run deploy-headless.sh first, then run the deployed check-extension-docs.sh, generate-context-line-counts.sh --check, and validate-context-index.sh against the now-deployed tree, and finally diff the source and deployed copies of the new file to confirm byte-identity.
